summary: A Java-based simulator for battles between character types from the Lord of the Rings universe, using object-oriented programming concepts and dynamic class scanning via reflection.
strengths: Appropriate use of OOP inheritance and polymorphism with a common Character base class and overridden kick and toString methods in subclasses.
Decoupled character creation via CharacterFactory using Reflections library to dynamically discover Character subclasses in the lotr package.
Comprehensive coverage of basic unit tests for individual character types verifying attributes, toString output, and bounds checks.
issues: Potential infinite loop in GameManager.java fight() method since fights between two Hobbit instances (0 power) or any zero-damage loop will never terminate.
Code duplication between King.java and Knight.java which both duplicate the static randomValue helper method and the private static Random instance.
Fragile class scanning in CharacterFactory.java which does not check if characterClasses is empty before calling rand.nextInt() and throws a generic RuntimeException on instantiation failures.
Missing package declarations in ElfTest.java, HobbitTest.java, KingTest.java, and KnightTest.java, which places them in the default package instead of package lotr.
recommendations: Implement a round limit or stalemate check in GameManager.java fight() method to prevent infinite loops.
Refactor King.java and Knight.java to inherit random attribute initialization from a common base class or helper to eliminate code duplication.
Add empty-check validation to CharacterFactory.java characterClasses list and provide more descriptive exception handling during reflection-based instantiation.
Add 'package lotr;' to all test files to properly align test packages with production code.
